description: Hi! I’m a student from Almaty, Kazakhstan, passionate about science, technology, research, and creativity. I’m participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge independently to challenge myself, explore new ideas, and develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.
summary: Hold the Outpost is a browser game for ages 7 to 12. You command a four-person base on Mars or the Moon and share too little power between life support, food, water, heat, shielding and radio. The Sun can be NASA's real space weather, loaded live from DONKI.
details:
Each sol (Mars day) the player splits power cells between machines, gives each astronaut a job, picks what to build and decides whether to spend a cell on a radio call to Earth. Mission Control warns when a solar storm may come. Hiding the crew costs a work day, not hiding costs radiation dose. The mission is won when the supply ship lands.
- Real Sun: three modes (game Sun, the last 40 days of NASA DONKI fetched live, and the May 2024 storm). Each sol is one real day. An X-class flare or a CME of 1,500 km/s or faster triggers a warning, and a DONKI SEP event that day is the particle storm. The game says this is its own rule, not a NASA forecast.
- Radio delay: on Mars the answer comes the next sol, on the Moon at once. Earth to Mars light time is estimated from JPL orbital elements.
- Offline: if DONKI is unreachable, the game uses an archive saved on 14 Nov 2026 and says so.
- Data screen: every real number with its source. Made-up game numbers are listed separately.
- For kids: a 6-step guided first mission, tap-to-explain terms, Russian and English, works on phones.
- Replay: four missions, random events, ten tasks with XP and ranks, an end report with a chart.
Tools: one HTML file (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas, SVG), no framework, no account, hosted on Vercel.
